title: Freddy 'Posey' Jenkins the showman
summary: Jenkins posed, twirled his trumpet, smoked cigars, played left-handed after a childhood accident, and drew audiences before Ellington did.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: Freddy was something, boy. Posing all the time, on stage, off stage, and always had a whole lot to say. He could talk the legs off an iron pot. And a little-bitty guy too. But he had personality-plus. And people come to see Freddy before they come to see Duke! They'd come in the theatre and they'd want to know, "Is Freddy Jenkins playing today?" -- playing any solos or this-that-and-the-other, you know.

Well, that's the way... See, it should have been that way with Johnny, but Johnny was so quiet and retiring... I mean, a lot of people come to the theatre just to see Johnny, too. But I mean, they weren't so outspoken about it. They'd come in, take a seat -- because they know Johnny is going to be there. But Freddy, boy, he'd be in the (?), he'd be waving his hand at somebody... I mean, he was really personality. He'd make you feel good.
I understand he was a left-handed trumpet player.

Yeah. Well, his right hand he lost his fingers, you know. He didn't have no fingers on his right hand. It got caught in a truck. I think it was the tail end of a truck coming down on it. As a kid, you know, it
chopped off his fingers. He had to play trumpet with his left hand.

Yeah. But that didn't stop him. Them fingers didn't stop him. And he could blow the trumpet, too. He could blow. And he'd twirl that trumpet around! Heh-heh! Oh, he was something. And he'd smoke a great big cigar. Yeah, Freddy Jenkins was something. Well, they used to call him "Posey" in the Duke Ellington Band.

Yeah, he was posin'. Posey, Posey. Oh, everything he did, man, was a picture. You know, he was posin' and carryin' on. He was something to see. I mean, he'd really make you feel good. Because you know, that's what you go a theatre for anyway, is entertainment. And when you'd get through seeing him, you know you was entertained.
